# Turning Backlog Into Bandwidth: How Bansal and Partners Reached 45% More Caseload With Lexi


Ashutosh


March 9, 2026


4 min read


“A single Friday brought us fifteen new matters, nine of them due in court by Monday. A year ago we would have taken three of the nine, because one draft alone used to eat a full working day. With Lexi, we drafted all nine in a day.” Sahil Bansal, Partner at Bansal & Partners


## **Key Highlights**


• Nine time-sensitive drafts, from banks, insurance fraud and recovery matters, completed and ready to file by Monday, from a single Friday intake


• 45% more caseload capacity since partnering with Lexi in October 2025, with no additional hiring


• 70% faster turnaround from first client contact to case assessment


• Every draft still reviewed by a lawyer before filing; Lexi builds the complete first draft, not just a first pass for someone else to finish


## **About the firm**


Bansal and Partners is a litigation practice led by Sahil Bansal, Partner, handling matters for banks and insurers, including insurance fraud and recovery suits. The firm takes on high volumes of deadline-bound work, often arriving from several clients in the same week.


This is deadline-driven, document-heavy litigation, where the work does not arrive evenly. It arrives in surges, and every matter in a surge is on its own clock.


## **Opportunity**


A single Friday could bring the firm fifteen new matters, several of them from banks and insurers with a court deadline the following Monday. Drafting one of those matters properly meant reading the policy, working through its terms, building the grounds for the case, and then checking the result line by line, even after a junior lawyer had done a first pass. That alone could take one person a full working day. Nine matters like that, arriving on the same Friday, could not all be done by Monday.


A year earlier, the firm’s honest answer to a Friday like that was to accept three of the nine and decline the rest. Not for lack of skill. For lack of hours. Turning away paying work was not a strategy. It was what the drafting bottleneck made unavoidable.


*“One draft used to take a full day for one person: reading the policy, working through the terms, building the grounds, then checking it line by line, even after a junior had done the first pass. On a week like that, saying no to work was the only responsible option.”*


**Sahil Bansal** , Partner at Bansal & Partners


## **Solution**


Lexi gave the firm a way to draft at the pace the work actually arrives, without lowering the bar on any single matter.


### **Nine drafts, one day**


On the Friday that would once have meant turning away six of nine matters, the firm drafted all nine, complete and ready for review, by Monday. The volume did not change. What the firm could do with it did.


### **A complete draft, not a first pass**


Lexi reads the policy and its terms and builds out the grounds for the case, producing a full first draft rather than a rough one for someone else to build on. A lawyer is reviewing and refining a draft, not assembling one from a blank page and a stack of documents.


*“Lexi reads the policy and the terms and builds the grounds the way we would ourselves. What lands on my desk is a draft to review, not a blank page to start from.”* · Sahil Bansal


### **Capacity without headcount**


Since partnering with Lexi in October 2025, the firm has taken on 45% more caseload without adding a single lawyer, and moves a matter from first client contact to case assessment 70% faster.


## **Impact**


The change shows up first in what the firm no longer has to say no to. A Friday that used to force a choice between nine deadlines and one day’s worth of drafting time no longer forces that choice at all.


The numbers, reported publicly, hold: 45% more caseload capacity and 70% faster turnaround from first contact to assessment, achieved without a single additional hire. For a firm whose work is banks, insurers and recovery matters, almost allof it deadline-bound, that is not a small efficiency gain. It is the difference between a firm that turns work away and one that does not.


*“Since October 2025 we have taken on 45% more caseload without hiring a single additional lawyer, and cases move from first contact to assessment 70% faster. The work we used to turn away because of one bad Friday, we just take now.”*


**Sahil Bansal** , Partner at Bansal & Partners
